```{r}
# ----- Metrics -----
log_loss <- function(y, p, eps = 1e-15) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, eps), 1 - eps)
  -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
}

brier_score <- function(y, p) {
  mean((p - y)^2)
}

acc_at_0_5 <- function(y, p) {
  mean((p >= 0.5) == y)
}

# ----- Stratified grouped K-fold for binary response -----
# Holds out entire participants while trying to balance the binary response rate across folds.
make_stratified_folds <- function(y, group, K = 5, seed = 0) {
  set.seed(seed)

  y <- as.integer(y)
  group <- as.character(group)

  if (!all(y %in% c(0, 1))) {
    stop("y must be binary 0/1.")
  }

  group_levels <- unique(group)

  if (length(group_levels) < K) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Number of groups (%d) is smaller than K (%d).",
      length(group_levels), K
    ))
  }

  # Group-level summaries
  group_summary <- data.frame(
    group = group_levels,
    n = as.integer(tabulate(match(group, group_levels))),
    n_pos = as.integer(tapply(y, group, sum)[group_levels])
  )

  group_summary$prop_pos <- group_summary$n_pos / group_summary$n

  # Randomize ties, then sort by response proportion so high/low subjects are distributed
  group_summary <- group_summary[sample(seq_len(nrow(group_summary))), ]
  group_summary <- group_summary[order(-group_summary$prop_pos), ]

  folds_groups <- vector("list", K)
  fold_n <- rep(0, K)
  fold_pos <- rep(0, K)

  global_prop <- mean(y)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(group_summary))) {
    this_n <- group_summary$n[i]
    this_pos <- group_summary$n_pos[i]

    # Greedily assign this participant to the fold that best preserves balance
    candidate_scores <- sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) {
      new_n <- fold_n[k] + this_n
      new_pos <- fold_pos[k] + this_pos
      new_prop <- new_pos / new_n

      # Balance response rate, with a tiny penalty for fold size imbalance
      abs(new_prop - global_prop) + 0.001 * new_n
    })

    k_best <- which.min(candidate_scores)

    folds_groups[[k_best]] <- c(folds_groups[[k_best]], group_summary$group[i])
    fold_n[k_best] <- fold_n[k_best] + this_n
    fold_pos[k_best] <- fold_pos[k_best] + this_pos
  }

  # Return row indices
  folds <- lapply(folds_groups, function(gs) {
    which(group %in% gs)
  })

  folds
}

# ----- CV wrapper for logistic GLMM: between-participant generalization -----
cv_glmm_kfold <- function(df, response, group, fixed_formula, random_spec,
                          K = 5, seed = 0,
                          optimizer = "bobyqa", nAGQ = 0) {
  # Sanity check for binary response
  uy <- sort(unique(df[[response]]))
  if (!all(uy %in% c(0, 1))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "%s must be 0/1, got: %s",
      response,
      paste(uy, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }

  df[[group]] <- as.factor(df[[group]])

  # Build model formula
  fml <- as.formula(
    paste0(response, " ~ ", fixed_formula, " + ", random_spec)
  )

  # Fit on full data, for final summary / AIC / BIC
  fit_full <- suppressWarnings(
    glmer(
      fml,
      data = df,
      family = binomial(),
      control = glmerControl(optimizer = optimizer),
      nAGQ = nAGQ
    )
  )

  # Grouped folds: all trials from a participant go into the same fold
  folds <- make_stratified_folds(
    y = df[[response]],
    group = df[[group]],
    K = K,
    seed = seed
  )

  rows <- vector("list", K)

  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    te_idx <- folds[[k]]
    tr_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(df)), te_idx)

    train <- droplevels(df[tr_idx, , drop = FALSE])
    test  <- df[te_idx, , drop = FALSE]

    # Keep held-out subject IDs as new levels
    test[[group]] <- factor(
      as.character(test[[group]]),
      levels = union(
        levels(train[[group]]),
        unique(as.character(test[[group]]))
      )
    )

    fit_k <- suppressWarnings(
      glmer(
        fml,
        data = train,
        family = binomial(),
        control = glmerControl(optimizer = optimizer),
        nAGQ = nAGQ
      )
    )

    # Between-participant prediction:
    # held-out subjects have no estimated random effects,
    # so use fixed effects only.
    p_test <- suppressWarnings(
      predict(
        fit_k,
        newdata = test,
        type = "response",
        re.form = NA,
        allow.new.levels = TRUE
      )
    )

    y_test <- test[[response]]

    rows[[k]] <- data.frame(
      fold = k,
      n_train = nrow(train),
      n_test = nrow(test),
      n_train_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(train[[group]]),
      n_test_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(test[[group]]),
      n_with_RE = 0,
      n_FE_only = nrow(test),
      mean_logloss = log_loss(y_test, p_test),
      brier = brier_score(y_test, p_test),
      acc = acc_at_0_5(y_test, p_test)
    )
  }

  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)

  avg <- colMeans(out[, c("mean_logloss", "brier", "acc")])

  list(
    cv_table = out,
    cv_avg = avg,
    fit_full = fit_full,
    cv_type = "between-participant grouped K-fold"
  )
}

```




## Execution guards (original CV functions above are unchanged)

```{r preflight}
check_grouped_cv <- function(d,response,binary=TRUE) {
  if(length(unique(d$Subj))<5) return("Fewer than 5 participants; no 5-fold CV.")
  if(anyNA(d[[response]])) return("Missing response values.")
  folds <- if(binary) make_stratified_folds(d[[response]],d$Subj,K=5,seed=0) else
    make_random_folds(d$Subj,K=5,seed=0)
  if(any(lengths(folds)==0)) return("Original fold allocator produced an empty fold; no algorithm change applied.")
  if(binary && any(vapply(folds,function(te) length(unique(d[[response]][-te]))<2,logical(1))))
    return("At least one training fold has only one response class.")
  NULL
}
legacy_binary_reason <- check_grouped_cv(df_allsubjs_test,"path_on_rim",TRUE)
legacy_ipi <- subset(df_allsubjs_test,!is.na(submitted_path_avgrt) & cond==1)
```

# Exp1_survey new analyses: risk predictor of binary rim-path use


```{r}

seed <- 0

RUN_GAMBLE_FRACTION_SENSITIVITY <- FALSE
RISK_MODE <- "full31"
RISK_PRESET <- "psm_usd450"

as_bool <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(logical(0))
  tolower(as.character(x)) %in% c("true", "1")
}

stopifnot(
  length(RISK_PRESET) == 1,
  "risk_ce_midpoint" %in% names(df_allsubjs_test)
)

# Raw CE in dollars.
# risk_ce_midpoint is the median of the two tested amounts
# immediately surrounding a valid switch.
# No normalization, centering, or scaling.
df_allsubjs_test$risk_ce_raw <-
  df_allsubjs_test$risk_ce_midpoint

new_results <- list()
new_status <- list()


run_covariate_family <- function(
    source,
    family_name,
    hard_only = FALSE,
    risk_predictor = "risk_ce_raw"
) {

  d <- source

  if (hard_only) {
    d <- d[d$cond == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  baseline <- if (hard_only) {
    "1"
  } else {
    "1 + cond"
  }

  baseline_no_cond <- "1"

  # Keep the supplied random-effects structure.
  # Risk is a participant-level fixed-effect predictor.
  re <- if (hard_only) {
    "(1 || Subj)"
  } else {
    "(1 + cond || Subj)"
  }

  risk_term <- risk_predictor

  candidates <- c(
    baseline = baseline,

    risk_no_cond = paste(
      baseline_no_cond,
      risk_term,
      sep = " + "
    ),

    risk = paste(
      baseline,
      risk_term,
      sep = " + "
    )
  )

  # Add interaction model as an additional candidate when not restricted to hard_only
  if (!hard_only) {
    candidates["risk_interaction"] <- paste0("1 + cond * ", risk_term)
  }

  # Use the same complete-case dataset for every candidate.
  required <- unique(c(
    "Subj",
    "path_on_rim",
    all.vars(as.formula(
      paste("~", candidates[["risk"]])
    )),
    all.vars(as.formula(
      paste("~", re)
    ))
  ))

  keep <- complete.cases(d[, required, drop = FALSE])
  d <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  d$Subj <- factor(d$Subj)

  write.csv(
    d,
    file.path(
      RESULT_DIR,
      paste0(family_name, "_analysis_rows.csv")
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  reason <- check_grouped_cv(
    d,
    "path_on_rim",
    binary = TRUE
  )

  if (
    is.null(reason) &&
    length(unique(d[[risk_predictor]])) < 2
  ) {
    reason <- "Risk predictor has no between-participant variation."
  }

  if (!is.null(reason)) {
    message(family_name, ": skipped: ", reason)

    new_status[[family_name]] <<- data.frame(
      family = family_name,
      status = reason,
      n = nrow(d),
      n_subjects = length(unique(d$Subj))
    )

    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # Original participant-grouped five-fold partitioning.
  fold_ids <- make_stratified_folds(
    d$path_on_rim,
    d$Subj,
    K = 5,
    seed = seed
  )

  assignment <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(
      seq_along(fold_ids),
      function(k) {
        data.frame(
          Subj = as.character(d$Subj[fold_ids[[k]]]),
          fold = k
        )
      }
    )
  )

  write.csv(
    unique(assignment),
    file.path(
      RESULT_DIR,
      paste0(family_name, "_folds.csv")
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  fits <- list()
  rows <- list()

  for (name in names(candidates)) {

    # Original CV fitting procedure.
    result <- tryCatch(
      cv_glmm_kfold(
        d,
        "path_on_rim",
        "Subj",
        candidates[[name]],
        re,
        K = 5,
        seed = seed
      ),
      error = function(e) e
    )

    if (inherits(result, "error")) {
      rows[[name]] <- data.frame(
        model = name,
        formula = candidates[[name]],
        status = conditionMessage(result),
        mean_logloss = NA_real_,
        brier = NA_real_,
        acc = NA_real_,
        AIC = NA_real_,
        BIC = NA_real_,
        singular = NA
      )

      next
    }

    fits[[name]] <- result
    fit <- result$fit_full

    convergence <- fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages

    status <- if (length(convergence)) {
      paste(convergence, collapse = "; ")
    } else {
      "ok"
    }

    rows[[name]] <- data.frame(
      model = name,
      formula = candidates[[name]],
      status = status,
      mean_logloss = unname(result$cv_avg["mean_logloss"]),
      brier = unname(result$cv_avg["brier"]),
      acc = unname(result$cv_avg["acc"]),
      AIC = AIC(fit),
      BIC = BIC(fit),
      singular = isSingular(fit)
    )

    write.csv(
      result$cv_table,
      file.path(
        RESULT_DIR,
        paste0(family_name, "_", name, "_cv.csv")
      ),
      row.names = FALSE
    )

    capture.output(
      summary(fit),
      file = file.path(
        RESULT_DIR,
        paste0(family_name, "_", name, "_summary.txt")
      )
    )
  }

  tab <- do.call(rbind, rows)

  tab$n <- nrow(d)
  tab$n_subjects <- length(unique(d$Subj))
  tab$risk_predictor <- risk_predictor

  print(tab)

  write.csv(
    tab,
    file.path(
      RESULT_DIR,
      paste0(family_name, "_comparison.csv")
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(
    fits,
    file.path(
      RESULT_DIR,
      paste0(family_name, "_fits.rds")
    )
  )

  new_results[[family_name]] <<- fits
}


# Audit why participants leave the risk cohort.
audit <- df_analysis_input[
  !duplicated(df_analysis_input$Subj),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

audit$has_submitted_maze <-
  audit$Subj %in% df_allsubjs_test$Subj

audit$risk_ce_valid <-
  as_bool(audit$risk_complete) &
  audit$risk_ce_censoring == "none"

audit$protocol_matches <-
  audit$risk_mode == RISK_MODE &
  audit$risk_preset == RISK_PRESET

# Safely check joint_model_eligible if present, otherwise default to TRUE
joint_eligible <- if ("joint_model_eligible" %in% names(audit)) {
  as_bool(audit$joint_model_eligible)
} else {
  TRUE
}

audit$analysis_included <-
  audit$has_submitted_maze &
  joint_eligible &
  audit$protocol_matches &
  audit$risk_ce_valid

audit$analysis_included[
  is.na(audit$analysis_included)
] <- FALSE

audit$reason <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(audit)),
  function(i) {

    x <- audit[i, ]
    reasons <- character()

    if (!isTRUE(x$has_submitted_maze)) {
      reasons <- c(
        reasons,
        "no submitted maze trials"
      )
    }

    if (!isTRUE(x$risk_ce_valid)) {
      reasons <- c(
        reasons,
        paste0(
          "risk CE: ",
          x$risk_ce_censoring,
          "; complete=",
          x$risk_complete
        )
      )
    }

    if (!isTRUE(as_bool(x$maze_complete))) {
      reasons <- c(reasons, "incomplete maze")
    }

    if (!isTRUE(as_bool(x$experiment_complete))) {
      reasons <- c(reasons, "incomplete session")
    }

    if (!isTRUE(as_bool(x$deadline_matches))) {
      reasons <- c(reasons, "deadline mismatch")
    }

    if (!isTRUE(x$protocol_matches)) {
      reasons <- c(
        reasons,
        "risk protocol mismatch"
      )
    }

    if (
      !length(reasons) &&
      !isTRUE(x$analysis_included)
    ) {
      reasons <- "other eligibility flag"
    }

    if (!length(reasons)) {
      "included"
    } else {
      paste(reasons, collapse = "; ")
    }
  },
  character(1)
)

write.csv(
  audit[, c(
    "Subj",
    "risk_ce_censoring",
    "risk_complete",
    "has_submitted_maze",
    "protocol_matches",
    "analysis_included",
    "reason"
  )],
  file.path(
    RESULT_DIR,
    "participant_selection_audit.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

print(as.data.frame(table(audit$reason)))


source <- df_allsubjs_test

source_joint_eligible <- if ("joint_model_eligible" %in% names(source)) {
  as_bool(source$joint_model_eligible)
} else {
  TRUE
}

eligible <-
  source_joint_eligible &
  source$risk_mode == RISK_MODE &
  source$risk_preset == RISK_PRESET

source <- source[
  !is.na(eligible) & eligible,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

run_covariate_family(
  source,
  "risk_only_both_conditions"
)


# Optional sensitivity analysis:
# replaces raw CE with fraction of draw choices.
if (RUN_GAMBLE_FRACTION_SENSITIVITY) {

  s <- df_allsubjs_test

  keep <-
    as_bool(s$risk_complete) &
    as_bool(s$maze_complete) &
    as_bool(s$experiment_complete) &
    as_bool(s$deadline_matches) &
    s$risk_mode == "full31" &
    s$risk_preset == RISK_PRESET

  s <- s[
    !is.na(keep) & keep,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  run_covariate_family(
    s,
    "gamble_fraction_sensitivity",
    risk_predictor = "risk_gamble_fraction"
  )
}

if (length(new_status)) {
  write.csv(
    do.call(rbind, new_status),
    file.path(
      RESULT_DIR,
      "new_model_skips.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```
